---
title: "What is SysNDD"
---

::: {.lead}
SysNDD is an expert-curated database of published gene-disease associations in neurodevelopmental disorders. This chapter explains the idea every page of the site is built on, the entity, and how SysNDD grades the evidence behind it.
:::

::: {.callout-note .who-can title="Who this is for"}
Everyone. Read this chapter before the task chapters. No account is needed to use the public site.
:::

## Why SysNDD exists

Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) include developmental delay, intellectual disability (ID) and autism spectrum disorder. They are clinically and genetically heterogeneous: many genes are involved, and new gene-disease associations are published every month.

Diagnostic laboratories and clinicians need an up-to-date, consistent answer to one question: *is there enough evidence that variants in this gene cause this disorder?* Answering it from the literature takes time and expertise. SysNDD collects that work in one place.

Clinicians and scientists with expertise in NDDs curate SysNDD. They read the published evidence, grade it with fixed [curation criteria](05-curation-criteria.qmd), and re-review older records as new papers appear. SysNDD continues the earlier SysID database [@kochinke_systematic_2016]; the [Preface](index.qmd) tells its history.

## The entity: gene, inheritance, disease

SysNDD does not grade genes. It grades **entities**. An entity is one gene, one mode of inheritance and one disease:

- the **gene**, identified by its HGNC identifier (HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee);
- the **mode of inheritance**, a term from the Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO), for example Autosomal dominant inheritance (`HP:0000006`);
- the **disease**, identified in OMIM (Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man) or MONDO (Mondo Disease Ontology).

A gene can therefore have several entities. Each one carries its own evidence category, because the evidence for one disease and inheritance says nothing about another.

*FBXO11* shows why this matters. On November 20, 2026 it had two entities in SysNDD:

| Entity | Inheritance | Disease | Evidence category |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sysndd:1848` | Autosomal dominant | Intellectual developmental disorder with dysmorphic facies and behavioral abnormalities (`OMIM:618089`) | [Definitive]{.cat .cat-definitive} |
| `sysndd:1998` | Autosomal recessive | intellectual disability (`MONDO:0001071`) | [Refuted]{.cat .cat-refuted} |

: The two *FBXO11* entities, accessed November 20, 2026. {#tbl-intro-fbxo11}

Heterozygous variants in *FBXO11* cause an established autosomal dominant disorder. A proposed autosomal recessive association with intellectual disability is not supported. A gene-level list would merge these two statements; the entity view keeps them apart.

Once created, an entity's gene, inheritance and disease do not change. If one of them must change, for example when the disease identifier changes, a Curator uses **Rename disease**: SysNDD creates a replacement entity, copies the review and status to it, and links the old entity to it. A duplicate entity is removed from use with **Deactivate entity**, which can also point to the entity that replaces it. Entities are never deleted, so their identifiers stay stable for citation.

## Evidence categories

Every entity within the NDD scope has one evidence category. Entities outside it are marked Not applicable (see below). The categories answer one question: how strong is the published evidence that this entity is a neurodevelopmental disorder?

| Category | In short |
| --- | --- |
| [Definitive]{.cat .cat-definitive} | The association is established by the published evidence. |
| [Moderate]{.cat .cat-moderate} | Better evidence than Limited, but not enough for Definitive. |
| [Limited]{.cat .cat-limited} | Published, and ID is indicated, but the genetic or clinical evidence is limited. |
| [Refuted]{.cat .cat-refuted} | The evidence argues against keeping the proposed association. |

: Evidence categories. The binding definitions are in the curation criteria. {#tbl-intro-categories}

These summaries are not the rules. Curators assign categories with the thresholds and conditions in [Curation criteria](05-curation-criteria.qmd).

### Not applicable

Some genes also have well-established disorders without intellectual disability or another neurodevelopmental feature. SysNDD keeps these entities for gene context and marks them [Not applicable]{.cat .cat-na}. The app shows this as "not applicable"; the curation criteria write `n.a.`.

Not applicable is not an evidence category and not a lower tier. It means the entity is outside the NDD scope, not that its evidence is weak.

### The NDD column

Tables show an **NDD** column with Yes or No. It records whether the entity's disease is a neurodevelopmental disorder. Both *FBXO11* entities above have NDD Yes.

## What SysNDD records for each entity

Beyond the category, an entity has a **review**: the curated evidence summary. A review contains:

- a **clinical synopsis**, a short summary of the reported phenotype;
- **phenotypes**, coded as HPO terms;
- **variation**, the variant types reported, coded as Variation Ontology (VariO) terms;
- **publications**, as PubMed identifiers (PMIDs), including GeneReviews chapters where they exist.

The category is stored as the entity's **status**. Reviews and statuses are written by Reviewers and Curators. A change becomes public only after a Curator or Administrator approves it. [Data model](04-database-structure.qmd) describes the data model in detail.

## Who uses SysNDD

| Reader | Typical tasks | Start with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clinicians and diagnostic laboratories | Check a gene's entities and categories; download a panel for variant filtering | [Find a gene](using-find-gene.qmd), [Build a gene panel](using-panels.qmd) |
| Researchers | Download tables, query the API, explore the analyses | [Get SysNDD data with the API and MCP](03-api.qmd), [Read the analyses](using-analyses.qmd) |
| [Reviewer]{.role} | Re-review assigned entities | [Re-review: guide for Reviewers](06-re-review-instructions.qmd) |
| [Curator]{.role} | Create, modify and approve entities; manage re-review | [Curation criteria](05-curation-criteria.qmd), then the Curator guide |

: Readers and where to start. {#tbl-intro-readers}

Searching, browsing, downloading and the analyses are open to everyone. An account is needed only to contribute; see [Your account](using-account.qmd).

## How SysNDD fits with other resources

SysNDD links each entity to standard identifiers, so its data can be combined with gene-, disease- and phenotype-centered resources. The Orphanet intellectual disability gene list (OrphaID, [id-genes.orphanet.app](https://id-genes.orphanet.app/ithaca/)) was curated in partnership with ERN ITHACA and SysID, the predecessor of SysNDD.

You can compare SysNDD with other NDD gene curation efforts, such as Gene2Phenotype, PanelApp and SFARI, under **Analyses › Compare curations**; see [Read the analyses](using-analyses.qmd).
